prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: 中文 · 用药说明 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 5 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "药品名称" · longest unbreakable word 20px · one-line width 108px
  col 2: header "规格" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 102px
  col 3: header "用法用量" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 109px
  col 4: header "频次" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 64px
  col 5: header "注意事项" · longest unbreakable word 31px · one-line width 521px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
An earlier design attempt for this table was rejected by independent reviewers. Their comments: another layout was rated poor: 注意事项列过窄，长段落被切成许多短行，首行尤其高；用法和频次相对宽松，空间分配失衡。 | another layout was rated acceptable: 注意事项比 A 易读，频次也较完整；但规格和用法列过窄，多处将剂量、单位或“口服”拆开。 | another layout was rated bad: 频次列极窄，“每日”和次数被拆成多行；药品名称也被切碎，影响逐行核对。 | your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: 注意事项有较多空间，频次基本完整；但规格和用法仍被挤成短行，剂量和给药方式不易一眼读清。 | another layout was rated poor: 注意事项较宽，但频次列把“每日”拆开，规格和用法也有明显碎行，影响用药信息的快速核对。 | another layout was rated acceptable: 频次保持较完整，注意事项有可读的行宽；规格和用法仍偏窄，多个剂量及“口服”被拆行。
another layout was rated acceptable: 注意事项有一定阅读宽度，频次也较易辨认；但用法用量很窄，口服和剂量被拆成多行。 | another layout was rated poor: 规格、用法和频次相对宽松，但注意事项过窄，长句被切成许多短行，主导了行高并妨碍阅读。 | another layout was rated acceptable: 注意事项和频次的分配尚可，行与行也容易区分；用法用量和规格仍有较多零碎换行。 | another layout was rated poor: 注意事项较易阅读，但药品名称和频次过窄；每日次数被拆成多行，药名也被频繁切断。 | your previous preferred design was rated acceptable: 注意事项有合理空间，频次保持可辨；不过用法用量中的口服和一次剂量换行零碎，规格也偏窄。 | another layout was rated acceptable: 注意事项比 A、C、E 更舒展，但频次被压窄，每日次数拆成多行，纵向比较不够顺畅。
